actions.text: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Hearings held. Hearings printed: S.Hrg. 119-46.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

dimensions.assessment: Affects U.S. persons engaged in critical mineral mining, refining, and recycling, as well as federal agencies and international allies.
dimensions.evidence: a United States person seeking to divest stock in mining, processing, or recycling operations for critical minerals

dimensions.assessment: Establishes formal federal oversight, reporting, divestment assistance, and international technology-sharing frameworks for critical minerals.
dimensions.evidence: Secretary may provide assistance to the person to find a purchaser that is not under the control of the government of a covered nation

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative costs for drafting comprehensive biennial reports and setting up assistance and technology strategies, but no funding sums are stated.
Imposes broad new reporting mandates, interagency consultations, divestment tracking, and international technology-sharing strategies.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, and every 2 years thereafter, the Secretary... shall submit to Congress a report

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent and recurring reporting requirements every two years, alongside ongoing technology strategies.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, and every 2 years thereafter

missing_information: Specific cost figures for preparing reports and executing technology-sharing strategies
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Department of the Interior to produce detailed global reports on critical minerals and rare earth elements, establish a divestment assistance process, and develop allied technology-sharing strategies.
